items.statement: Offering an orientation call and a hybrid video option will raise the proportion of starters who complete six or more sessions from 41 percent to at least 55 percent, with the largest gains among working people and those who rely on public transport.
items.rationale: Targets the early dropout and the suspected barriers; both adaptations can start without new evening hours.
items.risks: Barriers may differ from those assumed; video may reduce group connection.

items.statement: An evening group will raise completion among working people more than the other adaptations.
items.rationale: Work is a suspected barrier, but the evening group depends on unapproved staff hours.

items.statement: People who leave early have benefits at three months similar to those who complete, so completion alone understates the programme's reach.
items.rationale: No data exist on leavers; the finding would change how the clinic defines success.
items.risks: Low response from people who have left.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected because it does not depend on the unapproved evening hours.
